title: A regular sequence is Koszul-regular
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-module, $r\ge0$, and $f_1,\dots,f_r\in R$ such that for each $i=1,\dots,r$ multiplication by $f_i$ is injective on $M/(f_1,\dots,f_{i-1})M$. Then $f_1,\dots,f_r$ is $M$-Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], i.e. $H_i(K_\bullet(f_1,\dots,f_r)\otimes_RM)=0$ for all $i\neq0$, with $K_\bullet$ the Koszul complex of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. In particular every $M$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] is $M$-Koszul-regular, and every regular sequence in $R$ is Koszul-regular.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 062F (lemma-regular-koszul-regular, lines 7264-7298; its proof uses Lemma Tag 0629, lemma-cone-koszul, line 6751). Tags verified in tags/tags.

proof.text: Induct on r. For r=0, the exterior-power basis is indexed by powersetCard(Fin 0,n), which is empty for n>0. Therefore the positive tensor terms are subsingletons, and ExactAt.of_isZero and ExactAt.isZero_homology give positive homology vanishing directly.

For f : Fin (r+1) -> R let g be its prefix. Rewrite List.ofFn f as List.ofFn g appended with its final entry. Mathlib isWeaklyRegular_append_iff and isWeaklyRegular_singleton_iff give weak regularity of g and scalar injectivity of the last entry on M/(g)M. Apply the induction hypothesis to g and [lem-weil-pbc-koszul-tensor-zeroth-boundary-saturation] to that last entry.

Obtain the actual degreewise cone-coordinate equivalences and differential formulas from [lem-weil-pbc-koszul-tensor-cone-coordinates]. Convert the induction hypothesis homology vanishing into elementwise exactness via HomologicalComplex.exactAt_iff_isZero_homology and ShortComplex.moduleCat_exact_iff.

For a cycle x with coordinates (a,b), the first differential coordinate gives d a+t b=0. In degree one saturation supplies b=d c from t b=d(-a); in higher degree the second coordinate says d b=0 and prefix exactness supplies b=d c. Then a+t c is a positive prefix cycle, so write it as d z. The element with next-degree coordinates (z,-c) has boundary x, since its coordinates are (d z-t c,d c)=(a,b). The private cone_positive_exact theorem proves this entire chase. Translate elementwise exactness back to IsZero homology and finish the induction.

Keep the two existing corollaries: IsRegular.toIsWeaklyRegular supplies the module implication; for M=R, TensorProduct.rid gives a chain isomorphism with the untensored complex, which transports IsZero homology.
